exercises.instruction: 1–2 Classify each function as a power function, root function, polynomial (state its degree), rational function, algebraic function, trigonometric function, exponential function, or logarithmic function.

list.item: $$g(t) = \cos^{2}t - \sin t$$

exercises.instruction: 3–4 Match each equation with its graph. Explain your choices. (Don’t use a computer or graphing calculator.)

list.item: $$y = x^{8}$$ Details Three curves are graphed on the x y coordinate plane. The curve labeled f enters the bottom left of the viewing window in the third quadrant, goes up and to the right, concave down, briefly levels out at the origin, enters into the first quadrant, and continues rising to the right, now concave up. The curve labeled g enters the second quadrant at the top, goes down and to the right, concave up, and flattens near the origin, then goes up and to the right in the first quadrant, mirroring its earlier path. The curve labeled h resembles a U-shaped curve, enters the second quadrant to the left of curve g, goes down and to the right, then travels above the curve g after its intersection with curve g, reaches its low point at the origin, then goes up and to the right in the first quadrant by intersecting the first and the second curves, mirrors its earlier path, exiting to the right of the curves f and g.

$$y = \sqrt[3]{x}$$ Details Three curves are graphed on the x y coordinate plane. The curve labeled f enters the bottom left of the viewing window in the third quadrant, goes up and to the right, concave down, briefly levels out at the origin, enters into the first quadrant, and continues rising to the right, now concave up. The curve labeled g enters the second quadrant at the top, goes down and to the right, concave up, and flattens near the origin, then goes up and to the right in the first quadrant, mirroring its earlier path. The curve labeled h resembles a U-shaped curve, enters the second quadrant to the left of curve g, goes down and to the right, then travels above the curve g after its intersection with curve g, reaches its low point at the origin, then goes up and to the right in the first quadrant by intersecting the first and the second curves, mirrors its earlier path, exiting to the right of the curves f and g.

exercises.instruction: 5–6 Find the domain of the function.

problem.paragraph: $$f(x) = \frac{\cos x}{1 - \sin x}$$

list.item: Find an equation for the family of linear functions with slope $$2$$ and sketch several members of the family.
Find an equation for the family of linear functions such that $$f(2) = 1$$ . Sketch several members of the family.
Which function belongs to both families?

problem.paragraph: What do all members of the family of linear functions $$f(x) = 1 + m\left( {x + 3} \right)$$ have in common? Sketch several members of the family.
What do all members of the family of linear functions $$f(x) = c - x$$ have in common? Sketch several members of the family.
Sketch several members of the family of polynomials $$P(x) = x^{3} - cx^{2}$$ . How does the graph change when $$c$$ changes?

exercises.instruction: 11–12 Find a formula for the quadratic function whose graph is shown.

problem.paragraph: 11. Details An upward opening parabola is graphed on the x y coordinate plane. The parabola labeled f, enters the viewing window in the second quadrant near the y axis, goes down and to the right, crosses the y axis at (0, 18), reaches its vertex at (3, 0), then goes up and to the right through the labeled point (4, 2), and exits the top right of the viewing window. $$f(x) = 2x^{2} - 12x + 18$$

12. Details A downward opening parabola is graphed on the x y coordinate plane. The parabola labeled g enters the bottom left of the viewing window in the third quadrant, goes up and to the right through the negative x axis, passes through the labeled point (negative 2, 2), reaches its vertex in the second quadrant, goes down and to the right, crosses the y axis at the labeled point (0, 1), and then continues to go down through the labeled point (1, negative 2.5) in the fourth quadrant.
Find a formula for a cubic function $$f$$ if $$f(1) = 6$$ and $$f\left( {- 1} \right) = f(0) = f(2) = 0$$ .

Recent studies indicate that the average surface temperature of the earth has been rising steadily. Some scientists have modeled the temperature by the linear function $$T = 0.02t + 8.50$$ , where $$T$$ is temperature in $${}_{}^{}{}$$ and $$t$$ represents years since 1900.

list.item: What do the slope and $$T$$ -intercept represent?
Use the equation to predict the earth’s average surface temperature in 2100.

problem.paragraph: If the recommended adult dosage for a drug is $$D$$ (in mg), then to determine the appropriate dosage $$c$$ for a child of age $$a$$ , pharmacists use the equation $$c = 0.0417D\left( {a + 1} \right)$$ . Suppose the dosage for an adult is $$200$$ mg.

list.item: Find the slope of the graph of $$c$$ . What does it represent?
What is the dosage for a newborn?

solution.paragraph: $$8.34$$ , change in mg for every $$1$$ year change

problem.paragraph: The manager of a weekend flea market knows from past experience that if he charges $$x$$ dollars for a rental space at the market, then the number $$y$$ of spaces that will be rented is given by the equation $$y = 200 - 4x$$ .

list.item: Sketch a graph of this linear function. (Remember that the rental charge per space and the number of spaces rented can’t be negative quantities.)
What do the slope, the $$y$$ -intercept, and the $$x$$ -intercept of the graph represent?

problem.paragraph: The relationship between the Fahrenheit $$(F)$$ and Celsius $$(C)$$ temperature scales is given by the linear function $$F = \frac{9}{5}C + 32$$ .

list.item: Sketch a graph of this function.
What is the slope of the graph and what does it represent? What is the $$F$$ -intercept and what does it represent?

solution.paragraph: $$\frac{9}{5}$$ , change in $${}_{}^{}{}$$ for every $$1{}_{}^{}$$ change; $$32$$ , Fahrenheit temperature corresponding to $$0{}_{}^{}$$

problem.paragraph: Jade and her roommate Jari commute to work each morning, traveling west on I-10. One morning Jade left for work at 6:50 am, but Jari left 10 minutes later. Both drove at a constant speed. The graphs show the distance (in miles) each of them has traveled on I-10, $$t$$ minutes after 7:00 am.

list.item: Use the graph to decide which driver is traveling faster.
Find the speed (in mi/h) at which each of them is driving.

Find linear functions $$f$$ and $$g$$ that model the distances traveled by Jade and Jari as functions of $$t$$ (in minutes). Details Two lines are graphed on a coordinate plane. The horizontal axis t is labeled Time since 7.00 A.M. (minutes) and is displayed from 0 to 12 in increments of 3 units. The vertical axis y is labeled Distance traveled (miles) and is displayed from 0 to 30 in increments of 10 units. The line labeled Jade begins at the point (0, 10), goes up and to the right, and passes through the labeled point (6, 16). The line labeled Jari begins at (0, 0), goes up and to the right, and passes through the labeled point (6, 7).

problem.paragraph: The manager of a furniture factory finds that it costs $$\$ 2200$$ to manufacture $$100$$ chairs in one day and $$\$ 4800$$ to produce $$300$$ chairs in one day.

list.item: Express the cost as a function of the number of chairs produced, assuming that it is linear. Then sketch the graph.
What is the slope of the graph and what does it represent?
What is the $$y$$ -intercept of the graph and what does it represent?

solution.paragraph: $$13$$ ; cost (in dollars) of producing each additional chair

problem.paragraph: The monthly cost of driving a car depends on the number of miles driven. Lynn found that in May it cost her $$\$ 380$$ to drive $$480$$ mi and in June it cost her $$\$ 460$$ to drive $$800$$ mi.

list.item: Express the monthly cost $$C$$ as a function of the distance driven $$d$$ , assuming that a linear relationship gives a suitable model.
Use part (a) to predict the cost of driving $$1500$$ miles per month.
Draw the graph of the linear function. What does the slope represent?
What does the $$C$$ -intercept represent?
Why does a linear function give a suitable model in this situation?

problem.paragraph: At the surface of the ocean, the water pressure is the same as the air pressure above the water, $$15{lb} \slash {in}^{2}$$ . Below the surface, the water pressure increases by $$4.34{lb} \slash {in}^{2}$$ for every $$10$$ ft of descent.

list.item: Express the water pressure as a function of the depth below the ocean surface.
At what depth is the pressure $$100{lb} \slash {in}^{2}$$ ?

problem.paragraph: The resistance $$R$$ of a wire of fixed length is related to its diameter $$x$$ by an inverse square law, that is, by a function of the form $$R(x) = kx^{- 2}$$ .

list.item: A wire of fixed length and $$0.005$$ meters in diameter has a resistance of $$140$$ ohms. Find the value of $$k$$ .
Find the resistance of a wire made of the same material and of the same length as the wire in part (a) but with a diameter of $$0.008$$ meters.

problem.paragraph: The illumination of an object by a light source is related to the distance from the source by an inverse square law. Suppose that after dark you are sitting in a room with just one lamp, trying to read a book. The light is too dim, so you move your chair halfway to the lamp. How much brighter is the light?
The pressure $$P$$ of a sample of oxygen gas that is compressed at a constant temperature is related to the volume $$V$$ of gas by a reciprocal function of the form $$P = k/V$$ .

list.item: A sample of oxygen gas that occupies $$0.671m^{2}$$ exerts a pressure of $$39$$ kPa at a temperature of $$293$$ K (absolute temperature measured on the Kelvin scale). Find the value of $$k$$ in the given model.
If the sample expands to a volume of $$0.916m^{2}$$ , find the new pressure.

problem.paragraph: The power output of a wind turbine depends on many factors. It can be shown using physical principles that the power $$P$$ generated by a wind turbine is modeled by
where $$v$$ is the wind speed, $$A$$ is the area swept out by the blades, and $$k$$ is a constant that depends on air density, efficiency of the turbine, and the design of the wind turbine blades.

list.item: If only wind speed is doubled, by what factor is the power output increased?
If only the length of the blades is doubled, by what factor is the power increased?

For a particular wind turbine, the length of the blades is $$30$$ m and $$k = 0.214{kg}/m^{3}$$ . Find the power output (in watts, $$W = m^{2} \cdot {kg}/s^{3}$$ ) when the wind speed is $$10m/s$$ , $$15m/s$$ , and $$25m/s$$ .

problem.paragraph: Astronomers infer the radiant exitance (radiant flux emitted per unit area) of stars using the Stefan Boltzmann Law:
where $$E$$ is the energy radiated per unit of surface area measured in watts $$(W)$$ and $$T$$ is the absolute temperature measured in kelvins $$(K)$$ .

list.item: Graph the function $$E$$ for temperatures $$T$$ between $$100$$ K and $$300$$ K.
Use the graph to describe the change in energy $$E$$ as the temperature $$T$$ increases.

This wave pattern has three high points and two low points in this viewing window in such a way that it begins with a high point on the positive y axis, and exits above the positive x axis.

problem.paragraph: The table shows (lifetime) peptic ulcer rates (per $$100$$ population) for various family incomes as reported by the National Health Interview Survey.

list.item: Make a scatter plot of these data and decide whether a linear model is appropriate.
Find and graph a linear model using the first and last data points.
Find and graph the regression line.
Use the linear model in part (c) to estimate the ulcer rate for people with an income of $$\$ 25,000$$ .
According to the model, how likely is someone with an income of $$\$ 80,000$$ to suffer from peptic ulcers?
Do you think it would be reasonable to apply the model to someone with an income of $$\$ 200,000$$ ?

list.item: Find the regression line for the data.

problem.paragraph: Anthropologists use a linear model that relates human femur (thighbone) length to height. The model allows an anthropologist to determine the height of an individual when only a partial skeleton (including the femur) is found. Here we find the model by analyzing the data on femur length and height for the eight males given in the table.

list.item: Make a scatter plot of the data.
Find and graph the regression line that models the data.

problem.paragraph: It makes sense that the larger the area of a region, the larger the number of species that inhabit the region. Many ecologists have modeled the species-area relation with a power function. In particular, the number of species $$S$$ of bats living in caves in central Mexico has been related to the surface area $$A$$ of the caves by the equation $$S = 0.7A^{0.3}$$ .

list.item: The cave called Misión Imposible near Puebla, Mexico, has a surface area of $$A = 60m^{2}$$ . How many species of bats would you expect to find in that cave?
If you discover that four species of bats live in a cave, estimate the area of the cave.

problem.paragraph: The table shows the number $$N$$ of species of reptiles and amphibians inhabiting Caribbean islands and the area $$A$$ of the island in square miles.

list.item: Use a power function to model $$N$$ as a function of $$A$$ .

The Caribbean island of Dominica has area $$291{mi}^{2}$$ . How many species of reptiles and amphibians would you expect to find on Dominica? Island $$A$$ $$N$$ Saba 4 5 Monserrat 40 9 Puerto Rico 3,459 40 Jamaica 4,411 39 Hispaniola 29,418 84 Cuba 44,218 76

problem.paragraph: Suppose that a force or energy originates from a point source and spreads its influence equally in all directions, such as the light from a lightbulb or the gravitational force of a planet. So at a distance $$r$$ from the source, the intensity $$I$$ of the force or energy is equal to the source strength $$S$$ divided by the surface area of a sphere of radius $$r$$ . Show that $$I$$ satisfies the inverse square law $$I = k/r^{2}$$ , where $$k$$ is a positive constant.
